title: An Analysis of Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) as a Driver of Hoax Dissemination in the Prabowo Era Using MLP (Saputra, Heryati & Di Kesuma, Jurnal Kecerdasan Buatan dan Teknologi Informasi, 2026)
screen_reason: Primarily a classifier (MLP) paper, which the protocol normally excludes, BUT the sample description reports a descriptive content share with a real denominator: of 5,385 TikTok/Facebook comments scraped about the Prabowo-era government and manually labelled, 23% were labelled Hoax. That is a CONTENT prevalence (share of items in a sample classified false/misleading) in a non-balanced, scraped corpus, and the protocol says a study whose aim is something else is still included if a descriptive share is reported anywhere. Flagged borderline: a reviewer applying the 'detection/classifier work' exclusion strictly would exclude this paper.

estimates.country: Indonesia (Indonesian-language comments on the Prabowo administration)
estimates.date: not reported (article received 18 April 2026, published 2 May 2026)
estimates.measure_type: % of scraped TikTok/Facebook comments about the Prabowo-era government that were manually labelled 'Hoax'
estimates.value_raw: "23% are classified as Hoax and 77% as Non-Hoax" (of 5,385 comments)
estimates.denominator: 5,385 comments related to discussions about the Prabowo-era government, collected from TikTok and Facebook by web crawling with Apify
estimates.definition: Comment manually labelled Hoax 'based on information validity, including misleading content, exaggeration, and lack of credible sources'
estimates.misinfo_def: "Hoax and Non-Hoax, based on information validity, including misleading content, exaggeration, and lack of credible sources"
estimates.source_quote: The data distribution is imbalanced, where approximately 34% of the data belong to the FOMO category and 66% to Non-FOMO, while 23% are classified as Hoax and 77% as Non-Hoax.
estimates.page_loc: Section 2.2 Data Collection and Description, p. 130-131
estimates.ground_truth_detail: "The dataset is manually labeled into several categories based on predefined indicators" - no number of coders, no coder training, no inter-rater reliability reported; labels were then used as MLP training targets
estimates.moderator_quote: The dataset used in this study was obtained from TikTok and Facebook through web crawling using the Apify platform. A total of 5,385 comments related to discussions about the Prabowo-era government were collected.
estimates.notes: The 23% is stated as 'approximately'. The corpus is a topical scrape of comments on Prabowo-era government discussions, so the denominator is topical, not a general news or platform-wide sample; it is NOT a balanced or curated all-false dataset, which is why a prevalence reading is defensible. No sampling detail (which posts, which accounts, what date range) and no labelling reliability are reported, so the estimate is weakly documented. Year is the publication year; no data-collection window is given.

missed_or_uncertain: The 80:20 test split yields 269 Hoax of 1,077 test comments (25.0%) from the confusion-matrix text ('For the Hoax class, 199 out of 269 data were correctly classified' and 'the Non-Hoax class ... 761 out of 808'); this is a subsample of the same corpus and is not extracted as a separate estimate. The 34% FOMO share and all sentiment shares are not misinformation measures. All accuracy/precision/recall figures are model performance, not prevalence.

rob.design: Web-crawled convenience corpus of 5,385 Indonesian-language TikTok and Facebook comments on Prabowo-era government discussions (Apify); no date range, no post-selection criteria and no query terms reported; manual labelling into Hoax/Non-Hoax with unspecified coders and no inter-rater reliability; 80:20 train/test split for an MLP classifier; descriptive shares reported only in the sample description.
rob.item6_quote: Hoax and Non-Hoax, based on information validity, including misleading content, exaggeration, and lack of credible sources.
rob.item10_quote: The data distribution is imbalanced, where approximately 34% of the data belong to the FOMO category and 66% to Non-FOMO, while 23% are classified as Hoax and 77% as Non-Hoax.
